headline: Bets on a November BI hike and a soft rupiah push the 2Y up 9bp to 7.10% and the IGSYC 10Y to 7.69%, the top of its five-year history, despite softer CPI and lower Treasuries
summary: INDOGBs sold off for a third straight session, led this time by the 2–3Y sector: on PHEI's IGSYC curve the 1Y rose 6.3bp to 6.925%, the 2Y 9.1bp to 7.101%, the 5Y 7.5bp to 7.596% and the 10Y 6.2bp to 7.689%, the highest in the dashboard's history since October 2021 (the press puts it at a six-year high). The curve is flat at about 7.69% from 13 years out, and 1s2s steepened to 18bp as the market priced a BI hike. The 10Y benchmark FR0108 underperformed, rising 16.7bp to 7.793%, so it now sits 10bp cheap to the fitted curve. Sukuk held up again (the fitted PBS 10Y is 10.5bp through IGSYC and PBS034 13bp rich), and corporate credit stayed orderly: AAA 3Y is unchanged at 53bp over IGSYC, while BBB tightened to 255bp over AA from 266bp.
drivers: Front end prices a BI hike

The 2Y and 3Y rose 9bp each, the biggest moves on the curve, after Bank Permata's research team called a 25bp hike to 6.00% at BI's November meeting, citing the rupiah and a likely Fed hike in December (the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% last week with two members voting to raise). The IGSYC 1Y now sits 118bp over the 5.75% BI-Rate and 193bp over the 5.00% deposit facility. October CPI did not help: headline 3.23% (Reuters poll 3.29%, prior 3.28%) and core 2.56% (poll 2.75%) were both softer, but the market is pricing policy through the currency, not inflation.
Rupiah stuck near record lows, foreigners still selling stocks

JISDOR fixed at 18,161, up 0.13% on the day and within 0.2% of its 18,190 June record, while spot closed at 18,156 as most Asian currencies firmed. The JCI rebounded 0.8% to 5,097 on the first day of IDX's new rules dropping 81 concentrated stocks from the index, but foreigners still sold a net Rp376bn, taking 2026 equity outflows to about Rp126tn. Foreign SBN holdings were still about Rp917tn (13%) on Oct 27, so bonds have not seen a full exit yet, which is both the risk and the cushion.

The Ministry has seven SBN auctions left this year (four in November) and about Rp240tn targeted for Q4, after the Oct 27 SUN auction drew only Rp31.1tn of bids. Tuesday's sukuk auction offers PBS030, PBS034, PBS038 and PBS040 with a Rp10tn indicative target, which is the first test of demand at these yields. The 10Y FR0108 took the brunt today (+16.7bp, now 10bp cheap to IGSYC) while the 20Y FR0107 rose only 3.1bp.
US Treasuries: no help, and no blame

Friday's New York session took the US 10Y down 4bp to 4.94%, worth about −1bp for INDOGBs at the 1-year daily beta of 0.31; the INDOGB 10Y rose 6.2bp instead, so the whole move was local. Over four weeks the US 10Y is down 28bp while the INDOGB 10Y is up 45bp, and the weekly beta is −0.21. The INDOGB − UST spread has widened to 275bp, the 94th percentile of the year and near the top of its 190–299bp 52-week range.
data: October CPI (Nov 2)
Softer than expected and core is falling, so inflation alone does not force BI to hike; food and fuel keep the headline near the 3.5% ceiling.
October manufacturing PMI (Nov 2)
54.0 (p 52.4), strongest since March 2024
Growth is not the problem: record export orders and strong demand give BI room to tighten for the rupiah.
September trade balance (Nov 2)
Surplus US$3.36bn (f about US$1.5–2.3bn, p US$3.55bn); imports +18.4% y/y
A better surplus than forecast, but Jan–Sep surplus is down to US$10.6bn from US$33.5bn a year ago, so the rupiah leans more on portfolio money.
SUN auction (Oct 27)
Bids Rp31.09tn, awarded Rp20.65tn (target Rp30tn); FR0111 average 7.54%
Weak cover and a 30bp jump in the 10Y award in two weeks: the auction set a higher floor for secondary yields.
2026 budget outlook (late Oct)
Deficit 2.85% of GDP (budget 2.68%); net SBN Rp497.5tn (62.2%) issued by Sep
About Rp302tn of net SBN still to raise, while the 10Y trades about 80bp above the 6.9% budget assumption.
BI board meeting (Oct 21)
BI-Rate 5.75% (hold); deposit facility 5.00% (up); reserve requirement cut to 8% in Nov and 7% in Dec
Tighter at the very front, looser for bank lending. The market now expects the next step to be a BI-Rate hike.
MSCI market classification (Oct 15)
Consultation to move Indonesia from EM to Standalone; decision by Jun 30, 2027
The root of the foreign exit; it hits the rupiah first and bonds through the currency and risk premium.
view: The market has moved from pricing a foreign exit to pricing BI's response to it, and that keeps the front end and the 10Y heavy into the November board meeting: a 25bp hike is now the base case for some local banks, and until it comes or the rupiah stabilises, the selling has no natural stop. The quant side agrees: the Bond Flow Signal reads −0.74 (sell-off) for a sixth week, with the JCI slump, the rupiah and the 10Y's own momentum all bearish and only the 275bp spread to Treasuries arguing the other way, and the call is 53bp right since Oct 2. Its record argues for respect, not blind faith: since May 2022 it scores a Sharpe of 0.22 outright and 0.29 against Treasuries, with rally calls right 49% and sell-off calls 53% of the time, but since September 2024, when foreign flows took over, it scores 0.68 outright and 0.77 hedged; the US-trend variants score up to 0.88 but were chosen after the fact and are not live. Treasuries explain none of this: the weekly beta is −0.21 and the overnight read was −1bp against a +6bp local move, so a US rally will not rescue INDOGBs. I expect the 10Y to trade 7.55–7.90% over the next two weeks, with the top tested if JISDOR breaks 18,200 before BI acts. I stay underweight duration, would buy the belly only after BI has moved and the rupiah holds, and see the cheap FR0108 as the better long-end vehicle than the 20Y once the selling stops.

buckets.name: Front end 1–2Y vs BI-Rate
buckets.why: The IGSYC 1Y at 6.925% is 118bp over the 5.75% BI-Rate and 193bp over the 5.00% deposit facility; a 25bp November hike would leave it about 93bp over the new rate, which still prices some risk of more. The 2Y led today's sell-off (+9.1bp to 7.101%) and 1s2s steepened to 18bp from 15bp. PHEI history for this spread is only three days, so the meter is thin and the call rests on the policy gap. Previous call (add at 1Y 7.10%) still open: the 1Y is 17bp short of it.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add 1–2Y if the 1Y reaches 7.10% (a hike and more fully priced) or once BI has hiked and JISDOR holds below 18,000; avoid chasing below 6.80%.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y (FR0109)
buckets.why: The 5Y rose 7.5bp to 7.596% (+15bp in two sessions), and FR0109 (4.4Y) jumped 12.3bp to 7.659%, now 12bp cheap to IGSYC and the cheapest FR benchmark. The curve is steep to 5Y (2s5s 50bp) and flat beyond, so the belly has the best carry and roll. The level percentile rests on three stored PHEI days, so treat it as a guide only. Previous entry (7.55–7.60% once JISDOR held below 18,200 for three sessions) was not triggered: the rupiah condition is only two sessions old and yields gapped through the zone.
buckets.call: Move the entry to 7.65–7.75% on FR0109, triggered by a BI hike or three sessions of JISDOR below 18,200; target 7.35%, stop 7.95%.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 7.689% is at the 100th percentile of the past year (170 stored days, average 6.73%) and the highest since the series starts in October 2021, about 157bp above where 2026 began. The underweight is working (+6bp since Friday). It is cheap on history and on the 275bp spread to Treasuries (94th percentile), but the flow signal still reads sell-off, November brings four auctions and BI has not yet acted.
buckets.call: Stay underweight; turn neutral when the flow signal rises above −0.5 or after a BI hike that steadies the rupiah. A tactical long only above 7.85% with a stop at 8.05%.

buckets.name: 10s20s curve (FR0108 vs FR0107)
buckets.why: IGSYC 10s20s is flat at 0.1bp, leaving no term premium past 10 years. The benchmark steepener (buy FR0108, sell FR0107, entered at +7.8bp) was stopped today: FR0108 rose 16.7bp against 3.1bp for FR0107, so the spread swung to −5.7bp, through the 2bp stop. The 10Y benchmark is now 10.4bp cheap to IGSYC and FR0107 only 4.5bp, so the same trade is better value than before, but the stop comes first.
buckets.call: Closed at a stop (about −10bp of spread). Re-enter the FR0108/FR0107 steepener duration-weighted at −5bp or lower, target +5bp, stop −12bp.

buckets.name: PBS sukuk vs FR
buckets.why: The fitted PBS curve sits 10.5bp through IGSYC at 10Y (−9.8bp on Friday): PBS034 (12.6Y) is 13.3bp rich and PBS038 (23.1Y) 12.9bp rich, while PBS030 at the front is 3.7bp rich. The switch went against us today: FR0106 rose 10.4bp and PBS034 only 4.7bp, so the yield pick-up widened to 22bp from 17bp. The fit rests on four PBS series (low confidence), and both stored days show the same picture.
buckets.call: Keep the switch from PBS034/PBS038 into FR0106/FR0107 (22bp pick-up); Tuesday's Rp10tn sukuk auction should test PBS pricing. Close if the pick-up narrows to 10bp (target) or widens past 28bp (stop).

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AAA 3Y)
buckets.why: PHEI's AAA 3Y is unchanged at 53bp over IGSYC while AA widened 2.6bp to 85bp; BBB tightened to 255bp over AA from 266bp. Corporate spreads have not followed sovereign yields higher, because local banks and insurers dominate the buyer base. Only two stored days, so the spread history is short.
buckets.call: Hold AAA/AA; add only if AAA 3Y widens past 70bp. Avoid BBB until the rupiah stabilises.

watch: Next: the sukuk auction and US midterm elections (Tue Nov 3), the US Treasury refunding (Wed Nov 4), Q3 GDP (Thu Nov 5, f 5.0%, p 5.29%), October FX reserves and US payrolls (Fri Nov 6), then the remaining November SUN auctions, MSCI's November index review and BI's November board meeting; JISDOR 18,200 is the line that would bring a hike forward.
sources: Katadata (JCI close and foreign flows, Nov 2)
Kontan (SBN supply and foreign holdings, Nov 1)
